SPECIAL MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
MONDAY - SEPTEMBER 27, 2021 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
* COVID-19 NOTICE *
To protect public health and safety during the COVID-19 pandemic and in compliance with the current Los Angeles County Health Officer Order and City of Cerritos COVID-19 Safety Plan, the City Council Chamber will be open to the public. As authorized by State of California Executive Orders N-25-20, N-29-20, and N-08-21, and subsequently by Assembly Bill 361 (Chapter 165, Statutes of 2021), this meeting may also be conducted via teleconference, if necessary. Public observation and participation in this meeting will be facilitated through the methods described below.
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in-person in the Council Chamber subject to posted COVID-19 protocols.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in-person at the meeting or by using the following alternate methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

6.
Public Comments and Suggestions
This section is reserved for comments related to the Consent Calendar, Closed Session, and/or items not listed on the agenda but that are within the subject matter jurisdiction of the legislative body. Comments are limited to 5 minutes per person.
7.
Consent Calendar
Items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by one motion. Subject to the discretion of the legislative body, there will be no separate discussion of these items unless a legislative body member or citizen so requests, in which event the item may be removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately.

11.
Reports
11A.
Report from City Manager/Executive Director
During this part of the meeting the City Manager/Executive Director or designated staff will have an opportunity to report on various City matters and/or respond verbally to questions or comments from the prior City Council meeting, including any request by the City Council to provide a brief supplemental report or brief follow-up response to items from the prior City Council meeting's agenda.
11B.
City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Meeting Reports
During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. In addition, requests may be made of the staff for reports which will be presented to the City Council at a subsequent meeting, or for the scheduling of future agenda items. There will be no discussion or action taken on any of the items that may be presented during this agenda item.
12.

Closed Session Report
After the City Council/Successor Agency reconvenes into Open Session, designated City staff will provide a verbal report on any reportable action taken in Closed Session. This report will be memorialized in the official meeting minutes.
13.
Adjournment

MINUTES OF A SPECIAL MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD MONDAY,
SEPTEMBER 27, 2021, 7:00 P.M., IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL,
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Bruce Barrows
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Chuong Vo
  Mayor/Chair Grace Hu

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to excuse Council/Agency
  Member Naresh Solanki from the Monday, September 27, 2021, 7:00 p.m., City
  Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (4 – 0 - 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Solanki (excused)
  ABSTAIN:  None

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  Presentations

  None.

5B.  Informational update on the City's response to the COVID-19 pandemic and other City
  events, services, and programs.

  An informational report was given by Annie Hylton, City Librarian & Marketing Manager.
  A PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  There was no further action taken on this item.

5C.  Review and consideration of City Council appointments to fill vacancies for unexpired
  terms on the Cerritos Advisory Boards (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer.

  Mayor Hu offered her nomination of Judy Chiu to replace Mansour Meisami on the Fine
  Arts and Historical Commission.
 City of Cerritos  Monday, September 27, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting  Page 2 of 8

5.  Presentations/Appointments (continued)
5A.  (continued)

  Councilmember Yokoyama offered his nomination of Karen Wilson to fill the unscheduled
  vacancy on the Community Safety Committee.

  MOTION: It was moved by Hu, and seconded by Yokoyama, to approve Mayor Hu’s
  nomination of the following individual from the established eligibility list to replace Mansour
  Meisami for the remainder of the unexpired term on the Fine Arts and Historical Commission
  ending April 30, 2022 on the City’s Advisory Boards, as follows:

  Advisory Board  Name
  Fine Arts and Historical Commission  Judy Chiu

  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 – 0 - 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Solanki (excused)
  ABSTAIN:  None

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Hu, to approve Councilmember
  Yokoyama’s nomination of the following individual from the established eligibility list to fill an
  unexpired term ending April 30, 2022 on the City’s Advisory Boards, as follows:

  Advisory Board  Name
  Community Safety Committee  Karen Wilson

  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 – 0 - 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Solanki (excused)
  ABSTAIN:  None

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Written correspondence:
  (Written correspondence is considered public record and full-text copies of submitted
  written correspondence can be obtained in the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer)

  Edward Stanila submitted written correspondence related to Consent Calendar Item 7.C.
  requesting the City Council purchase electric zero-emission mowers from an alternate
  vendor.

  In-person comments:

  Case Van der Linden spoke regarding tree removals and the current drought conditions.

  Anantha Ramachandran spoke regarding uneven sidewalks in the community and
  upcoming Cerritos municipal election dates.
 City of Cerritos  Monday, September 27, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting  Page 3 of 8

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions (continued)

  Jay Gray spoke regarding tree removals and an alleged trip and fall incident in the
  community.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to provide public comment, the
  Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

7.  Consent Calendar

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Monday, September 13, 2021, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting
  Minutes (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Yokoyama, to approve the Monday,
  September 13, 2021, 7:00 p.m., City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting Minutes
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (4 – 0 - 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Solanki (excused)
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of the Register of Demands

7B.1. Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated September 27, 2021 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Yokoyama, to approve the
  Register of Demands as follows:

  City of Cerritos  September 27, 2021  $1,847,680.86 (COUNCIL)

  The motion carried (4 – 0 - 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Solanki (excused)
  ABSTAIN:  None

7C.  Award of contract for the purchase of two commercial grade 48” riding lawn mowers,
  Bid No. 1436-21 (COUNCIL).

  This item was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration at the
  request of Councilmember Yokoyama.

  A staff report was provided by Kanna Vancheswaran, Director of Public Works/Water &
  Power.

  Written correspondence was submitted for this item and read into the record during
  Agenda Item No. 6. The following information is listed under Agenda Item No. 6 and is
  cross referenced below.

(minutes continue on the next page)
 City of Cerritos  Monday, September 27, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting  Page 4 of 8

7.  Consent Calendar (continued)

  Written correspondence:
  (Written correspondence is considered public record and full-text copies of submitted
  written correspondence can be obtained in the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer)

  Edward Stanila submitted written correspondence requesting the City Council purchase
  electric zero-emission mowers from an alternate vendor.

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Yokoyama, to award a contract
  for the purchase of two commercial grade 48” riding lawn mowers to Diamond A.
  Equipment in the amount of $42,763.28 (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 – 0 - 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Solanki (excused)
  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

  None.

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of the City of Cerritos City Charter (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer. A PowerPoint presentation
  was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Written correspondence:
  (Written correspondence is considered public record and full-text copies of submitted
  written correspondence can be obtained in the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer)

  Martin Grossman submitted written correspondence regarding Council member term
  limits and requested additional community outreach for future Charter review meetings.

  In-Person comments:

  Anantha Ramachandran requested the City Council introduce a ballot measure to restrict
  those elected to City Council to two-term lifetime limits.

  Jay Gray expressed support for introduction of a proposed ballot measure to restrict
  those elected to City Council to two-term lifetime limits. He also spoke regarding other
  items that could be addressed in the City Charter such as limitations on campaign
  contribution and the City Treasurer position.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to provide public comment, the
  Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

(minutes continue on the next page)
 City of Cerritos  Monday, September 27, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting  Page 5 of 8

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9A.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to:

  1. Schedule two (2) additional City Charter Review Study Sessions, to be noticed as
  City Council Special Meetings, in the evening hours at either the Cerritos Library or a
  similar City facility meeting space; and

  2. Include notification of the meetings to each registered voter household in Cerritos
  and through all available City media outlets (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 – 0 - 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Solanki (excused)
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration of the 2021-22 Mayor’s annual appointment recommendations
  for resident and community member service on external committees (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared the public comments period
  closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Barrows, to continue review and
  consideration of the 2021-22 Mayor’s annual appointment recommendations for resident
  and community member service on external committees to the Thursday, October 14,
  2021, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 – 0 - 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Solanki (excused)
  ABSTAIN:  None

9C.  Review and consideration of award of contract for Water Division SCADA Automation
  Control System Services, RFP No. 1430-21 (COUNCIL).

  Staff reports were given by Javier Martinez, Water Superintendent, and Kanna
  Vancheswaran, Director of Public Works/Water & Power. A PowerPoint presentation was
  displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared the public comments period
  closed.

(minutes continue on the next page)
 City of Cerritos  Monday, September 27, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting  Page 6 of 8

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9C.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Hu, to:

  1.  Award a professional services contract for the Water Division SCADA Automation
  Control System Services, RFP No. 1430-21, to Macros Automatics Corporation in the
  amount of $241,362.50 and reject the other proposals received; and

  2.  Approve the expenditure of funds in the amount of $241,362.50 from the City’s
  approved Fiscal Year 2021-2022 operating budget; and

  3.  Authorize the Mayor to execute the agreement on behalf of the City of Cerritos; and

  4.  Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any contract modifications
  that may be necessary to complete the specified scope of work (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 – 0 - 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Solanki (excused)
  ABSTAIN:  None

9D.  Review and consideration of award of contract for Bloomfield Avenue street
  improvements, Project No. 22301, Bid No. 1437-21 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Dario Simoes, Assistant City Engineer. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared the public comments period
  closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Hu, to:

  1. Award a contract for the Bloomfield Avenue Street Improvements (Total Bid), Project
  No. 22301, Bid No. 1437-21, to Sequel Contractors, Inc. in the amount of $627,200,
  and reject the other bids; and

  2. Approve the expenditure of $600,000 in Measure “M” funds from Capital
  Improvement Project No. 22301; and

  3. Approve the expenditure of funds from Project No. 14099: Program/Parkway Planter
  Block Wall Improvements as a source of funding for Alternate #2 in the amount of
  $25,000; and

  4. Approve the expenditure of funds in the amount of $2,200 from anticipated savings
  in other Capital Improvement Program projects approved for FY 2021-2022 for the
  remaining balance to complete the subject project; and

  5. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any project-related change
  orders (COUNCIL).
 City of Cerritos  Monday, September 27, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting  Page 7 of 8

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9D.  (continued)

  The motion carried (4 – 0 - 1) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Solanki (excused)
  ABSTAIN:  None

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation.

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or
  Federal legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.

  None.

11.  Reports

11A.  Report from City Manager/Executive Director

  An informational update regarding the City’s recycled water service to residential
  customers was given by Art Gallucci, City Manager/Executive Director, Javier Martinez,
  Water Superintendent, and Kanna Vancheswaran, Director of Public Works/Water &
  Power. This verbal report was in response to a public inquiry at a recent City Council
  meeting. There was no City Council action taken on this matter.

11B.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Meeting Reports

  Reports were given by Mayor Pro Tem Vo and Councilmember Yokoyama.

12.  Closed Session

  Bill Ihrke, City Attorney, announced the City Council would not recess to Closed
  Session to discuss the following items as listed on the Closed Session agenda:

  12A.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957 (COUNCIL)
  Title: City Manager

  12B.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957 (COUNCIL)
  Title: City Attorney

  12C.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957 (COUNCIL)
  Title: City Clerk/Treasurer
 City of Cerritos  Monday, September 27, 2021, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Special Meeting  Page 8 of 8

13.  Adjournment

  The meeting adjourned at 9:19 p.m.

  /s/Vida Barone
